title: Euler's theorem on Eulerian circuits and trails, and Petersen's 2-factor theorem
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the classical characterization of Eulerian graphs and of Petersen's 2-factor theorem, for finite simple graphs. (1) Euler–Hierholzer: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if every vertex has even degree, and the circuit can start at any prescribed vertex. (2) Eulerian trails: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian trail if and only if it has 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree; when the odd vertices are exactly a and b, there is an Eulerian trail from a to b. (3) Eulerian orientations: if every degree is even, the edges can be oriented so that every vertex has equal in- and out-degree. (4) Petersen's 2-factor theorem (1891): every finite 2k-regular graph is the edge-disjoint union of k spanning 2-regular subgraphs. The proof of (4) is built on (1)–(3): the graph is decomposed into edge-disjoint closed trails (using the closed-trail lemma behind the Euler theorems), oriented along them, and the resulting k-regular digraph is split into k permutations by Hall's marriage theorem; each permutation yields a 2-factor. Mathlib already contained the necessity directions of (1) and (2); their sufficiency directions were listed there as open TODO items.
